detailed_description:
First-person POV, one single continuous handheld take with no cuts; the camera is my own eyes, a tired father, and no other adult is ever near the camera. The only part of me ever visible is my own two bare hands and forearms in the lower frame; exactly two hands, never more. Sarah always looks the same: a girl of about five, shoulder-length brown hair, a blue long-sleeve top, dark grey leggings, cream velcro sneakers, a yellow plastic star bracelet on her left wrist. Photorealistic early-1990s live-action film still, shot on 35mm film with a real lens, practical sets and real physical materials: scuffed rotomolded plastic, vinyl padding, cheap carpet, nylon rope net. Natural textures and real-world scale. Flat cool fluorescent light from a drop ceiling, a loud ordinary room. Visible film grain, slight halation around lights.
Motion: the camera moves like a real person's head and body. Every move starts with a small anticipation, eases in and eases out, travels on a gentle arc and settles with a little follow-through; nothing snaps or jitters. People move with weight. The last half second holds almost still on the end state.
Exactly one child close to me, and only at the end: Sarah, a girl of about five with shoulder-length brown hair, a blue long-sleeve top, dark grey leggings and cream velcro sneakers. The children at the far tables are small and always moving: eating pizza, laughing, running, waving balloons. No adult anywhere in frame.

[Shot 1] In order: 1. 0-1 s: I sit at the party table, my left hand resting a paper soda cup with a plastic lid and a straw on the paper tablecloth; behind it the room is busy and loud. 2. 1-3.5 s: my head pans slowly left to right on a gentle arc, easing in and out: kids at the far tables eating pizza and laughing, a child waving a balloon, two kids running between the tables, the yellow-poled play structure and the ball pit at the back of the room. 3. 3.5-4.5 s: as the pan settles, Sarah walks up to me from the right, holding a yellow paper birthday crown in both hands, her steps small and quick. 4. 4.5-5 s: she stops right beside my chair, lifts the crown toward me, and holds.
The shot ends on: Sarah standing beside my chair on my right, holding a yellow paper crown up toward me with both hands; my left hand with the soda cup on the table; the busy party and the play structure behind her.

overall_soundscape:
Party din, kids shrieking and laughing, arcade bleeps, a distant birthday song, fluorescent hum, ice rattling in the soda cup.

non_diegetic_music:
None.
